As an exercise for myself I started trying to formalize some results from a textbook on representation theory and noticed that there doesn't appear to be a type in mathlib for equivalencies of representations (i.e. G-linear isomorphisms).

One could avoid needing such a thing by using Representation.asModule and Representation.ofModule to translate representations into modules and then just use LinearEquiv, but this doesn't seem to fit with the spirit of how the rest of the api for representations is constructed. For example, with G-linear maps we have Representation.IntertwiningMap which extends LinearMap with the additional intertwining condition.

Is there any interest in (or perhaps even anyone already working on) an analogue to IntertwiningMap, but which extends LinearEquiv rather than LinearMap? Something like a Representation.IntertwiningEquiv?
Argh, that's embarrassing. It seems the version of mathlib in my project is a few weeks old, sorry about that.
yeah this PR (#36127) got merged in less than 48 hours!
